score_evidence: 'Universal SIM (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, and more)' -> deployment_awareness_absence: the shipping product is architecturally bound to commercial carriers
'1 Month Cloud Storage' + LinkedIn specialties listing 'aws' -> deployment_awareness_absence: commercial cloud video backend, with zero mention of ATO/RMF/IL4/STIG/CMMC anywhere in ~1665 words

blind_spots.blind_spot: Commercial-carrier dependency baked into the shipping product, while the DoD use case is precisely where commercial carriers do not exist
blind_spots.operator_reality: At an austere or OCONUS perimeter there is no Verizon/AT&T/T-Mobile tower to roam onto. The Phase II proposes standing up private 4G/5G, but the RangeCam that actually ships auto-selects a commercial network — meaning the fielded article and the demo article are two different systems, and the private-network variant carries spectrum authorization, frequency deconfliction and RF interference approvals nobody on a 10-person consumer-hardware team owns.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Seven thousand rural US customers all sit inside commercial coverage, so carrier availability has never been a design constraint — the site even sells against it with a coverage-check map.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Barn Owl Cameras connect to all major and rural cellular networks automatically. No tech savvy required!

blind_spots.blind_spot: AWS-backed cloud video and alerting with no visible accreditation path
blind_spots.operator_reality: Video from a base perimeter is at minimum CUI and its aggregate reveals security-force posture. Putting it in a commercial AWS tenant with a consumer retention policy means an IL4/IL5 boundary, STIG-hardened components, a POA&M and a named ISSO before a single camera goes live on a DoD network. That accreditation timeline routinely exceeds the period of performance remaining on the transition contract — the exact failure mode where months-to-field outruns funded months.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The commercial business monetizes cloud retention as a subscription tier ($7-$15/mo), so cloud is the revenue model, not an architecture decision to be revisited for government.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 1 Month Cloud Storage / Unlimited Storage for Favorited Images

blind_spots.blind_spot: Over-the-air firmware push marketed as a headline feature, which is a configuration-management stopper on an accredited network
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Skip the drive' means the vendor can silently change software on a device sitting inside a base security perimeter. On an ATO'd system every firmware change is a configuration-control event requiring signed code, change board approval and re-testing; an auto-update channel to a vendor cloud is a supply-chain finding that will be written up before fielding, not after.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: In the consumer market OTA update is a pure cost saver and a competitive differentiator — the comparison table lists it as a win over competitors, so nobody has been asked what it looks like to a security control assessor.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Remote Firmware Updates: Skip the Drive

opener_hook: Your 2022 Phase II with Patrick SFB's 45 SFS scoped surveillance across 70 square miles, while the RangeCam that ships today routes video to cloud storage over a universal commercial SIM — those are two different accreditation problems, and only one of them has a customer waiting.
what_they_do: Sells solar-powered, cellular, off-grid AI security cameras to ranchers and landowners, with one Air Force Phase II adapting the kit for base-perimeter security forces.
